_note: The curated 'Human Story' route: the largest turning points, in chronological order, one line each. Only chapters whose exhibit the canonical timeline has already reached are ever shown; the route simply ends where the player's timeline stands.
title: The Human Story

chapters.line: It begins with a body learning to stand.
A stone struck on purpose. An edge that did not exist before.
Toolmaking becomes a habit — and it will never stop.
Long legs, bigger brains, and the first walks out of Africa.
A shape held in the mind, then found in the stone.
Fire kept alive. The night pushed back.
Our species appears — across Africa, not in a single place.
Words. Knowledge can now outlive the one who found it.
Shells strung to be worn: objects that carry meaning.
One species spreads across a planet.
Out of sight of land, people cross the sea.
Animals appear on stone, lit by firelight.
The last great continents are reached.
Clay, transformed by fire, holds water.
In several places at once, people begin to plant.
Animals are kept, not hunted.
Fire pulls metal out of rock.
Tens of thousands of strangers, living together.
A disc on an axle. Loads begin to roll.
Speech becomes visible. Memory moves outside the body.
An alloy worth crossing continents for.
A few dozen signs, one for each sound.
The common metal, in every farmer's hand.
Value, stamped and counted.
From a few axioms, everything else — by proof.
Cheap sheets from plant fibre. Knowledge becomes light.
Eurasia becomes one conversation.
Nothing becomes a number.
Stars, swells and birds guide voyagers across the widest ocean.
A needle points north, whatever the sky.
A thousand identical copies. Knowledge escapes.
Every inhabited continent, joined by sea — at terrible cost.
Look closer. Measure. Publish. Be proved wrong.
One law for the falling apple and the orbiting Moon.
Machines begin to do the work of muscle.
Heat becomes motion, anywhere.
A mild infection protects against a deadly one.
Messages at the speed of electricity.
All life, one family tree.
The night is switched on.
Fifty-nine seconds in the air. The sky becomes a road.
Space and time bend.
Infections that killed for all of history become curable.
A machine that can become any machine.
A switch smaller than a grain of rice — soon, smaller than dust.
Life's instructions, written in four letters.
Something made by people circles the Earth.
Footsteps on another world.
Networks join into one network.
Anyone can publish; anyone can read.
The accumulated knowledge of humanity, in a pocket.
Machines begin to learn from what we have written.
